The '''2023–24 Süper Lig''', officially called the '''Trendyol Süper Lig 2023–24 season''', was the 66th season of the [[Süper Lig]], the highest tier [[Association football|football]] league of [[Turkey]].

The fixtures were announced on 18 July 2023 at 21:30 (UTC+3).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=201&ftxtID=41684 |title=Trendyol Süper Lig Fikstür Çekimi Yarın Yapılacak |publisher=Turkish Football Federation |access-date=17 July 2023 |date=17 July 2023 |language=tr |archive-date=17 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230717150529/https://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=201&ftxtID=41684 |url-status=live }}</ref> The defending champions [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] successfully retained their title.

On 12 December 2023 it was announced that the league was suspended indefinitely following [[Ankaragücü]] president [[Faruk Koca]]'s punching of referee [[Halil Umut Meler]] after their home match against [[Çaykur Rizespor|Rizespor]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13028415/ankaragucu-president-punches-referee-two-detained-as-turkish-super-lig-game-descends-into-chaos-after-full-time |title=Turkish football leagues suspended indefinitely after Ankaragucu president punches referee |access-date=2023-12-12 |archive-date=2023-12-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231212134822/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13028415/ankaragucu-president-punches-referee-two-detained-as-turkish-super-lig-game-descends-into-chaos-after-full-time |url-status=live }}</ref> However, on 13 December 2023, the same day Meler was discharged from the hospital, it was agreed that league games would resume on 19 December. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Turkish referee Halil Umut Meler leaves hospital after attack from Ankaragucu president Faruk Koca {{!}} Super Lig matches to resume on Tuesday |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13029364/turkish-referee-halil-umut-meler-leaves-hospital-after-attack-from-ankaragucu-president-faruk-koca |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=[[Sky Sports]] |language=en |archive-date=2023-12-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213151132/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13029364/turkish-referee-halil-umut-meler-leaves-hospital-after-attack-from-ankaragucu-president-faruk-koca |url-status=live }}</ref>

While [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] held the record for the most points in a season by collecting 93 points in the [[1988–89 1.Lig|1988–89 season]], Galatasaray became the new owner of this record by collecting 102 points, sealing the final 3 points with a win against [[Konyaspor]] that handed them both the title and the first Süper Lig 100-point season.

Galatasaray improved the longest winning record with 17 wins in a row between weeks 19 and 36.

Fenerbahçe previously held the record for the most wins in a season with 29 wins in the 1988–89 season. Galatasaray became the new owner of this record with 33 wins. Fenerbahçe played 36 matches, achieving 29 wins, 6 draws, and 1 loss, with an average of 2.58 points per match, making them the team with the "best performance" in the Süper Lig. Galatasaray broke this record this season by playing 38 matches, achieving 33 wins, 3 draws, and 2 losses, with an average of 2.68 points per match, becoming the new holders of the "best performance" record.

==Teams==
A total of 20 teams contest the league, including 17 sides from the [[2022–23 Süper Lig|2022–23 season]] and [[2022–23 TFF First League]] champions [[Samsunspor]], runners-up [[Çaykur Rizespor|Rizespor]] and play-off winners [[Pendikspor]]. Rizespor immediately returned to top level and Pendikspor is competing in the Süper Lig for the first time in their history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Çaykur Rizespor, Spor Toto Süper Lig'de - Ligler Haber Detay Sayfası TFF |url=https://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=204&ftxtID=41282 |website=tff.org |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=tr |archive-date=20 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620222810/https://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=204&ftxtID=41282 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Pendikspor Futbol A.Ş. Spor Toto Süper Lig'de - Spor Toto 1. Lig Haber Detay Sayfası TFF |url=https://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=287&ftxtID=41448 |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=tff.org |language=tr |archive-date=9 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609070131/https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=287&ftxtID=41448 |url-status=live }}</ref> Samsunspor returned to top level after 11 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spor Toto 1. Lig'de 2022-2023 Sezonu Şampiyonu Yılport Samsunspor Oldu - Spor Toto 1. Lig Haber Detay Sayfası TFF |url=https://tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=287&ftxtID=41082 |website=tff.org |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=tr |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603183226/https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=287&ftxtID=41082 |url-status=live }}</ref>
The bottom four teams will be relegated to the [[TFF First League|2024–25 TFF First League]].

===Changes from last season===

[[Ümraniyespor]] was the first team that had been relegated to [[2023–24 TFF First League]] after a 2-1 loss to [[MKE Ankaragücü|Ankaragücü]] at away on 21 May 2023, ending its one-year stay in [[Süper Lig]]. The second team relegated was [[Giresunspor]], who sealed their fate due to [[İstanbulspor]]'s 4-0 win against Ümraniyespor at home on 7 May 2023 despite a 2-0 win to [[Antalyaspor]] at home on same day and ended their two-year stay in the top flight.

The first promoted team was [[Samsunspor]] whose 4–1 won home against [[Keçiörengücü]] on 23 April 2023 confirmed their return to Super Lig after eleven years. The second team that got promoted is [[Çaykur Rizespor]], who a goalless draw with [[Altınordu F.K.|Altınordu]] on 21 May 2023 and returned to the top flight immediately. The third and final team to qualify for Süper Lig was [[Pendikspor]]. After defeating [[Bodrumspor]] 2–1 in play-offs final on 8 June 2023 at [[Akhisar]], Pendikspor entered the top flight for the first time in the club's history.

Thanks to Turkey's improved ranking (12th place at the end of the 2022-23 season), the Süper Lig return to qualifies 5 teams in European football instead of 4; 2 in [[2024-25 UEFA Champions League]] (the champions will enter the playoff round and the runner-up will enter the second qualifying round), 2 in [[2024-25 UEFA Europa League]] (the winner of the [[2023-24 Turkish Cup]] will enter the playoff round and the team in third place will enter the second qualifying round), and 1 in [[2024-25 UEFA Conference League]] (the team in fourth place will enter the second qualifying round)
